items.quote: Project order book is normally 24 to 30 months.

items.statement: Most project contracts have price variation clauses to pass on raw material increases
items.quote: Yes, these contracts, most of them have price variation clauses.

items.statement: Navy framework agreement worth Rs. 17-18 crores, type tests completed, supply to continue for 20-30 years
items.quote: The Navy business was a framework agreement for all new types of pumps, which we have introduced in the fleet and after this framework that means the type tests are done, the shipyards can order these for all subsequent ships. So the framework agreement was for about Rs. 17-Rs. 18 crores.

items.statement: R&D spending roughly $2 million equivalent across businesses annually
items.quote: R&D is a constant process for us across all our businesses. Roughly, we would be spending about 2 million across our businesses, $2 million or euros or something.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin of 15-20% with a good Speciality-commodity balance, as envisaged during Dahej CAPEX.
items.quote: we would expect EBITDA of between 15% to 20% and that is what we were envisaging when we made the CAPEX at Dahej.

items.statement: No significant CAPEX planned; only minor debottlenecking for Boron business costing less than Rs. 10-15 crores.
items.quote: Yeah, very little CAPEX. It will be some debottlenecking type of thing, but nothing significant.

items.statement: Good visibility in most segments except agrochemicals; Speciality chemical volumes were very poor in FY23 and FY24.
items.quote: certainly from a volume point of view, financial year 23 and 24 was very poor for the Speciality chemicals.

items.statement: Speciality chemicals target 20%+ margins; commodity margins range from zero to +/-5%. New products target 30% margin.
items.value: 20% and up for specialities; zero plus minus 5% for commodity
items.quote: for the special ities, 20% and up is the number ; while for the commodity it could be anything, it could be zero plus minus 5

items.statement: Topline reduction driven by lower raw material prices; delta between selling price and raw material cost improved marginally.
items.quote: although we reduced our top line, the delta between the selling price and the cost of raw materials has in fact improved a little bit

items.statement: Most sectors showing recovery except agrochemicals where worst is over; Europe remains challenging, US and India better.
items.quote: All sectors, as I mentioned, apart from the agrochemical sector, seem to be doing better. Again, we are not experts on any particular sector.

items.statement: Current revenue split 50:50 Speciality:non-Speciality; long-term target is two-thirds Speciality, one-third commodity.
items.quote: right now it's about 50 :50, b ut if you take the long -term average before we made the investment at Dahej, it was two-thirds Speciality and one-third commodity

items.statement: Agrochemical sector (10-12% of revenue, mostly Speciality) had near-zero demand; Chinese dumping and Red Sea logistics disrupted supply.
items.quote: whatever business we had for the agrochemical sector has been near zero.

items.statement: Repaying Rs. 2 crores monthly; aim to eliminate all fixed term debt in 3 years assuming no further CAPEX.
items.quote: we are paying back about Rs. 2 crores every month and depending on our cash flow, we will be reducing the debt.

items.statement: Dedicated plant expansion requires 3 years from environmental clearance; multipurpose plants quicker but still need permissions.
items.quote: from day zero it would be 3 years before you could actually have commercial output in case of dedicated plants.

items.statement: Boron business can reach Rs. 150 crores from current CAPEX with minor debottlenecking; overall business Rs. 450-500 crores at current raw material prices.
items.quote: we believe that we could do about Rs. 150 crores from our current scale of CAPEX, just from the Boron business.

items.statement: Speciality chemicals capacity utilization at ~50%; bulk chemicals above 90%. Automotive Speciality product successful in commercial trials, ramping up over next few quarters.
items.quote: in the Speciality chemicals while I don't have an exact number and it depends on product to product, but I would say we are at about 50% capacity.

items.statement: Added two directors: Haren Parekh (finance) and Kuldeep Tiwari (operations); Dahej site received Responsible Care Certificate.
items.quote: We also added another person, Mr. Kuldeep Tiwari, as an Executive Director to head our operations and he brings with him a couple of decades of operating experience

items.statement: Installed LPG replacing furnace oil; turbine at Roha using waste heat recovery reduces grid dependence; Dahej >90% energy self-reliant.
items.quote: We've installed LPG for one of our operations replacing furnace oil, that's a much cleaner burning fuel and we continue on our journey towards self-reliance in energy.

items.statement: Ambernath land sale (Rs. 5 crores) delayed due to buyer permissions; not in company's control.
items.quote: this is unfortunately not in our hands, and it depends on permissions that the buyer needs to get and things like that

items.statement: Management avoids forward-looking topline/bottomline projections; will discuss quarterly. FY25 recovery uncertain but visibility good except agrochemicals.
items.quote: It's difficult to predict and I don't like to make forward -looking projections on top line or bottomline. We'll take it, as you know, we'll discuss every quarter

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% plus for FY25 with margins commensurate and order inflow target of INR 8,000-10,000 crores (around INR 9,000 crores)
items.value: 20%+ revenue growth; INR 8,000-10,000 cr order inflow
items.quote: Revenue growth, as we have been maintaining, it will be 20% plus in terms of revenue. Margin also will be commensurate to that. And order inflow, we're expecting the order what we can see in our horizon goes to INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores say INR9,000 crores, our target is to have this year's order inflow.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected around 10% plus, difficult to improve significantly beyond that in construction industry
items.quote: It's difficult. You see, construction industry has got their own standard margin and revenue. So 10% plus is, I think, okay. If we can do something better, we'll be happy, we'll try that. But I think we have to live with this margin, 10%, a little bit more than 10%.

items.statement: Target 30% of revenue from overseas in 2-3 years; currently pursuing overseas opportunities with 20%+ share expected in near term
items.quote: We aim to do around 30% of revenue from overseas by another 2 years' time or 3 years' time. Now today, the kind of job which we're pursuing, if we get some of them, I think it will be around 20% plus on our overseas business.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected around INR 250 crores, lower than last year's INR 450+ crores due to prior TBM and trench cutter investments
items.quote: Capex will be less than last year because last year or second last year we had to invest for the tunnel boring machines and trench cutters. So it was more than INR450 crores plus I think last year. This year it could be around INR250 crores in that range

items.statement: Order book as of March 2024 is a little under INR 20,000 crores; new orders secured in FY24 were about INR 6,900 crores
items.quote: During the year, we have secured new orders of about INR6,900 crores. And our order book as of March '24 is a little under INR20,000 crores.

items.statement: Strong pipeline of INR 25,000-30,000 crores across domestic and overseas, with 50-50 split in marine segment; submitted bids around INR 20,000 crores
items.quote: I can see around INR25,000 crores to INR30,000 crores jobs in different stage either in tender or we submitted and tender to come they come in 6 months, 7 months' time.

items.statement: Top 8 projects contribute 80% of revenue; focusing on bigger jobs (INR 1,000-3,000 crores) with fewer players and better qualification
items.quote: If you see today, our work in hand, we may have 50 jobs in hand. And out of that, about eight contribute to 80% of our revenue. So the moment you go for the bigger jobs, you have less players.

items.statement: No major legacy project issues remaining; Bangalore Metro completed, only claims/arbitration left which would be upside
items.quote: Yes, as far as the projects are concerned, we had Bangalore Metro as all of you know that is in the last two quarters before it has been behind us. So, what is remaining now only is the claim and arbitration.

items.statement: Overseas contracts typically fixed price with escalation built into bid price; mobilization advances of 10-15% received on recent overseas jobs
items.quote: See, basically in foreign contract, escalation normally you have to cover in your price. That is what we see in foreign contract.

items.statement: TBMs depreciated over 5-6 years; working capital cycle sustainable at current levels with payments received on time per contract terms
items.quote: The TBMs are depreciated. The current ones that we have in use are being depreciated over a period of five to six years.

items.statement: Management expects ~10% topline growth in FY25, targeting around Rs. 4,800 crores revenue, with potential to reach Rs. 5,000 crores if CV and car industries grow.
items.quote: More or less we are saying that we will go by 10% this year on the topline. So, that would come out to a number of Rs. 4,800 crores, around that number.

items.statement: Overall volume target of 20 million wheels in FY25 versus 19 million in FY24.
items.quote: On numbers, we are looking at 20 million wheels this year versus 19 million last year.

items.statement: Domestic CV industry expected flat to tepid growth in FY25 due to election year and monsoons.
items.quote: we all know that this is an election year and so there is, we have seen a slight slowdown in the CV industry so far and this is going to be followed by monsoons. last year we did the highest CV volume. This year our forecast is ranging from a flat year to somewhat tepid growth

items.statement: Domestic aluminum wheel business projected to grow ~10% in FY25 based on past nominations.
items.quote: On the domestic aluminum wheel side, we expect about a 10% growth. This is based on our past performance, past projects that we have been nominated for.

items.statement: Two-wheeler EV wheel business targeted to grow ~16% in FY25.
items.quote: And there we are leaders now for wheels and they are in much better value addition on these wheels and this business should grow about 16%.

items.statement: Passenger car steel wheel business projected to grow 10.6% in FY25 after regaining projects.
items.quote: So, but this year I am glad to tell you that we are projecting a 10.6% growth in the steel wheel for passenger cars.

items.statement: Tractor business expected to grow ~12% in FY25 driven by market share gains from new LTAs.
items.quote: So, here I can say with prominence that our tractor share of business is going to go up this year and this means about 12% growth in revenue in terms of volume and obviously value also will follow suit.

items.statement: Export business expected to grow ~10% in FY25 with new OTR product lines gaining traction in Europe and America.
items.quote: We expect this to grow by another 10% this year and in the export business we're adding new product lines like off-road vehicle wheels.

items.statement: Aluminum knuckles revenue to start from September, targeting ~Rs. 35 crores in FY25, then more than double and 4x thereafter.
items.quote: We should start our revenue growth from September onwards. Revenue is coming in from knuckles perhaps a little bit earlier and this year we should be doing close to about if I am not mistaken, about Rs. 35 crores in revenue and then going forward, we expect this revenue to go more than double and then after that, this revenue to go more than 4x.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at ~Rs. 225 crores, to be funded entirely from internal accruals with no fresh borrowing.
items.quote: In terms of overall CAPEX, which was there on the table, I think for next year was in the range of Rs. 225 odd crores which can be funded entirely from the accruals, and nothing needs to be borrowed from the outside market.

items.statement: New alloy wheel capacity expansion planned near Maruti in Punjab/Haryana, timing FY26-FY27.
items.quote: So, FY26, FY27, yes, but we would definitely need to come closer to Maruti. So, I am just giving you a heads up and all to the investor community that we may be coming up with a new factory in Punjab, very close to Maruti.

items.statement: EBITDA per wheel expected to improve above FY24's Rs. 253 due to favorable mix (alloy, export, tractor) and price correction in passenger car steel wheels.
items.quote: 253 was the number last year, so definitely you will see a much better number than 253.

items.statement: Price correction agreed with major OEMs on passenger car steel wheels (70-80% of business), effective from April 1, impact visible in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: Once that happens, you will see the impact of that itself in the first quarter. So, because that will be backdated from 1st of April.

items.statement: Debt peaked at Rs. 1,048 crores as of March 2024; scheduled repayments of ~Rs. 105 crores annually for next 3 years plus potential prepayments from accruals.
items.quote: So, as we guided last time that the debt that you are seeing as on March 24 is the peak debt in our books and subsequently it should taper down.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis impact largely absorbed; customers adjusted inventories and freight advantage vs Asian competitors persists.
items.quote: Customers have adjusted their inventories. So, there will be other dynamics rather than the Red Sea issue that will come into play.

items.statement: Alloy wheel order book visibility extends to 2027; Maruti nomination secured with potential 20-25% market share over 2-3 years.
items.quote: I have an order book in front of me that is extending up till 2027. I see the numbers. I see the possibility of expanding my market beyond India.

items.statement: AMW acquisition completed; equipment being relocated to Jamshedpur for CV capacity expansion of ~400,000 wheels operational by June.
items.quote: We are adding a new CV capacity of almost 400,000 wheels that is coming from equipment that was lying in AMW. We're not letting the equipment idle. We're just moving that equipment to other parts of our locations where they're already producing in mass.

items.statement: Target INR 1,000 crores revenue from India over next 5 years
items.quote: We remain optimistic on building our India presence with 2 brands, both Himeya and Atmosphere, and we continue to want to achieve revenues of approximately INR1,000 crores from India over the next 5 years.

items.statement: Aim to reach full capacity utilization in 18-24 months
items.quote: We would like to head in that direction and be running at full capacity over the next 18 months or so, 18 months, 2 years kind of time frame, if not earlier.

items.statement: Current capacity can support revenue of just over INR 4,000 crores
items.quote: Approximately INR4,000 crores, just over INR4,000 crores, is our estimate.

items.statement: EBITDA margin typically operates in 18-22% band in stable conditions
items.quote: And the band of EBITDA that I've shared with investors and other stakeholders, we typically operate in the 18% to 22% band depending on product mix and timing and market conditions.

items.statement: Demand environment stable with slight negative bias in major markets
items.quote: So the absolute demand remains stable. I would say, there is an overhang of caution in major markets. So I'm using the word stable with a slight negative bias, if you will, at least in major markets.

items.statement: Growth to be driven by broader product mix, larger client mix, and more markets served
items.quote: And therefore, we will endeavor to continue to enhance -- to continue to grow, will be driven by a broader product mix, larger client mix, and more markets that we serve.

items.statement: Lost revenue from Bed Bath & Beyond wind-down and exited non-core product categories losing INR 200 crores
items.quote: We've also pulled out of some categories of products, which I've shared with stakeholders earlier, we lost INR200 crores on that front because we don't see that as core going forward.

items.statement: No major capex planned beyond annual maintenance and organic requirements
items.quote: We don't have any plans for any additional capex of any consequence other than our annual maintenance and organic capex requirements and something we've shared very openly and clearly with stakeholders.

items.statement: Plan to raise equity sometime this fiscal to strengthen balance sheet
items.quote: So keeping all of these things in line, we would like to strengthen and raise equity sometime this fiscal, that's what we're running for.

items.statement: Target net debt to EBITDA below 3.5x and DSCR in 1.8x-2.2x range
items.quote: So we would like to bring our net debt to EBITDA levels to below 3.5x, which is where we used to be. And so we would like to head there. And we would like to make sure that our DSCRs are in the region of 1.8x to 2.2x.

items.statement: Focus on growth, deleveraging, and strengthening equity over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes, focusing on growth, focusing on deleveraging, and focusing on strengthening equity. These are the 3 things I would like to focus on, and that's what we've shared with stakeholders.

items.statement: Brand demand similar to private label, no higher demand for brands
items.quote: I don't see much movement. I think that the same logic that applies to private label in terms of demand would apply to the world of brands.

items.statement: Working on reducing working capital cycle time but no specific target disclosed
items.quote: Well, see, that's something I wouldn't want to specifically spell out. But I would say that we are working to be better our current cycle time.

items.statement: Peak revenue was INR 3,200+ crores in FY22, aim to return to that level and grow beyond
items.quote: Our peak revenues were about INR 3,200 plus crores in FY '22, and then we lost some steam post some of the macro issues that the market faced. And so we want to head back in that direction and then onwards from there.

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 sales turnover guidance of INR1,500-1,600 crores with blended EBITDA margin of 16%
items.quote: we are looking for a sales turnover of over INR1500 to INR1600 crores on consolidated basis and margins should be now to 16% on blended basis

items.statement: Full capacity consolidated revenue target of INR1,700-1,800 crores when all plants fully operational
items.quote: From our subsidiaries and it can be on a console basis we are looking for a sales of about INR1,700 crores to INR1,800 crores when all the plants will be fully operational

items.statement: FY25 capex plan of INR70-80 crores including solar installation and maintenance, expansion capex to be finalized soon
items.quote: roughly, as of now, we are having the capex plan about INR70 to INR80 crores, but for capacity expenses we will come out with the plans very soon

items.statement: Warangal unit capex of INR600 crores spent out of envisaged INR650 crores, third rPET line operational by June 2024
items.quote: we have spent over about INR600 crores on our Warangal unit and almost all the plants have been operating, except this rPET granule line, which is expected to be operational by end of next month

items.statement: Legacy business order book visibility only 1-2 months, textile sector recovery expected from August onwards
items.quote: in our legacy business order book is not of 3 months and 4 months. It is hardly 1 to 2 months only, but we are seeing the improvement in the sector from August onwards

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 11.72%, down 101 bps QoQ due to finished product price slide without input price adjustment
items.quote: We earned EBITDA of INR. 27.79 crores during Q4 FY24, dropped to 11.72% by 101 basis points over Q3 FY24 EBITDA margins of 12.73%

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 15.40%, up 137 bps QoQ with subsidiaries contributing INR19.27 crores EBITDA
items.quote: EBITDA margins at 15.40% have improved by 137 basis points. In absolute terms, we achieved revenue of INR 305.53 crores and earned EBITDA of INR47.06 crores

items.statement: Warangal unit achieved operating profits over 22% in Q4 FY24 with improved capacity utilization
items.quote: We achieved a very good set of numbers from our Warangal plant where we achieved operating profits of more than 22% during the quarter

items.statement: Textile sector recovery expected around July-August 2024, legacy business maintaining 11%+ EBITDA margins
items.quote: we are looking for the recovery in the textile sector which seems to be happening around July and August month

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting from 65% textile to 50% packaging and 50% textile/technical textile in next 1-2 years
items.quote: going forward, say, in the next one or two years, we are seeing almost 50% contribution in sales will be from the packaging sector, 50% from the textile and technical textile sector

items.statement: HDPE/PP recycling delayed due to pending FSSAI/EFSA food-grade regulations and unorganized sector competition
items.quote: the regulation for approval from FSSAI for food safety of HDPE, PP is still pending. The FSSAI and EFSA both are not very much clear

items.statement: QIP and preferential warrants proceeds used to repay all working capital borrowings and term debt, achieving near zero debt status
items.quote: On the back of funds raised at the recent QIP as well as preferential warrants issue, we have set off entire working capital borrowings as well as repaid term debt of the holding company achieving almost zero debt status currently

items.statement: Third rPET granule line (14,000 tons) expected operational by June 2024, taking total rPET capacity to 42,000 tons
items.quote: 3rd line is also expected to be operational by June end

items.statement: New capacity commissioning timeline 15-18 months from approval, expansion plans to be finalized soon
items.quote: it takes about 15 months to 18 months' time to commission the new facility fully operational

items.statement: Warrant conversion period up to September 2025, no conversion planned in FY25
items.quote: the warrant currency is for 18 months and we have allotted the warrants in January itself. So, the 18-month period is up to September 25. So, based on the requirement of the funds, we will convert the warrants in trenches also we can, but as of now there is no plan to convert in this financial year

items.statement: Next two years focus on consolidating North, East, Central corridors; next three years entering South and West
items.quote: The next two years are going to be more consolidating in the North, East, Central corridor, and the next three years also entering South and West.

items.statement: Customer GTV grew 7% YoY to Rs 1.08 lakh crore in FY24, second consecutive year above Rs 1 lakh crore
items.quote: It's been a relatively flat year because of headwinds in the AePS business. So only a 7% growth , 107,000 crores compared to 100,000 crores in the previous year .

items.statement: Service fee gross margin grew 10% YoY to Rs 169 crore in FY24 from Rs 154 crore in FY23
items.quote: Service fees, the main number that we track,which has grown from Rs. 154 crores the previous year to Rs. 169 crores in the last financial year .

items.statement: EBITDA of Rs 14.2 crore and PAT of Rs 12.1 crore achieved at consolidated level for continued and Spice Money business in FY24
items.quote: We have achieved an EBITDA of Rs. 14.2 crores for the financial year and a PAT level of Rs. 12.1 crores at consolidated level .

items.statement: Cash and Cash-out GM contribution declined from 77% to 68%; Collections grew from 8% to 14%; Subscription packs now 6%; Banking 2%
items.quote: If you look at our core business of Cash and Cash out, it's declined from a GM contribution point of view from 77% to 68%. And we have seen new product lines, especially if you look at collections, our contribution of collections to gross margin has grown from 8% to 14%.

items.statement: Cash Management Services GTV grew 54% YoY to Rs 27,682 crore in FY24; large CMS Adhikaris up 23% to 7,300 contributing 90% of GTV
items.quote: So, we are close to Rs. 27,000 crores in FY'24. This is the gross transaction value of the collections made from the branches compared to Rs. 18,000 crores in the past year .

items.statement: Bharat Bill Payment System GTV grew 90% YoY to Rs 4,190 crore; EMI loan repayments grew 2.4x to Rs 3,160 crore; repeat customer base nearly 50%
items.quote: year-on-year overall while we have grown 90% in customer GTV Rs. 4,190 crores compared to Rs. 2,210 cr ores which is about 1.9x growth. Within this EMI , loan repayments have grown 2.4x year-on-year, Rs. 3,160 crores from Rs. 1,325 crores

items.statement: AePS industry declined 6% due to 2FA implementation and issuer bank transaction limits; Spice Money GTV declined only 5%, gaining market share to 17.53% in Q4
items.quote: In FY'23, if you look at the industry, it did about the Off-Us part of the industry, FY'23 was about Rs. 3,33,000 crores and in FY'24 that's dropped 6% to Rs. 3,14,000 crores.

items.statement: Lifetime merchant base reached 1.4 million (14 lakh) with 4 lakh monthly transacting; 55% CAGR over 5 years from 240,000 in FY20
items.quote: to -date lifetime we have onboarded about 14 lakh small merchants, who we refer to as Spice Money Adhikaris on our web and app platform, majority of them use our mobile app to deliver ATM and other financial services to c onsumers in rural India

items.statement: Planning to enter lending business via strategic NBFC acquisition to create credit products for merchants and small businesses in Emerging India
items.quote: In our board meeting recently where we adopted the financial results for last year , we have also passed a resolution and made the necessary announcements where we are looking to enter the lending business through a strategic NBFC acquisition within the company.

items.statement: Lifetime CASA accounts opened crossed 3.5 lakh; Q4 saw 16,000 Adhikaris each opening 5+ accounts; focus on float and cross-sell
items.quote: Lifetime now we have opened over 3 lakh accounts in semi -urban and rural and what we are tracking here is growth in float in terms of people using these accounts.

items.statement: Third-party lending facilitated nearly 100,000 loans lifetime; key learnings: inherent credit demand, need for customized products with friendly repayment, erratic supply from partners
items.quote: We have seen significant learning. So more than the number s, I would encourage you to look at the box where we're talking about our three key learnings, right.

items.statement: Credit business is long-term (10-20 years); will build brick-by-brick with no short-term number commitments; focus on product innovation, physical proximity, enhanced risk management
items.quote: This is a business over the next 10 to 15 to 20 years that we want to build, and we will build it like brick-by-brick, block-by-block.

items.statement: Changed device capitalization policy in FY24; previously capitalized devices and provided right-to-use to Adhikaris, now expensed
items.quote: This is basically a change in capitalization policy because till FY'23, we were capitalizing the devices and providing a right -to-use to the Ad hikaris. This is something that we changed as a policy in FY '24

items.statement: No short-term numbers committed; building long-term business over 10-20 years brick-by-brick
items.quote: I will not commit to any short-term numbers here. This is a business over the next 10 to 15 to 20 years that we want to build, and we will build it like brick-by-brick, block-by-block.

items.statement: FY25 AePS business muted; focus on counter share; collections growing steadily
items.quote: I think that effectively this year is going to be little mute in terms of the impact on the A ePS business, but our growth is going to be to grow counter share and that's what we're going to focus on

items.statement: No AUM target for FY25; focus on completing NBFC acquisition and testing products in Q4
items.quote: So, I don't think we put any AUM target for this financial year. I think our focus is going to be first to complete the process of acquisition and once that's done, we're going to start by a few products which we know have worked on the marketplace that we can work with our own capital and we're going to test out those products with the NBFC.

items.statement: UPI wallet pilots planned for Q2 FY25
items.quote: So UPI wallet in the Q2 is where we see us being ready to run some pilots around the wallet.

items.statement: Significant tech and innovation budget allocated for FY25 and FY26, mainly hiring tech talent
items.quote: I think in this coming year and the next year, we have actually allocated a good number for tech and innovation and it's mainly in the form of hiring tech talent.

items.statement: EBITDA doubled from Rs 10.2 cr to Rs 21.7 cr in FY24 due to gross margin improvement and lower indirect costs
items.quote: So that has improved EBITDA almost by 100% from Rs. 10.2 crores to Rs. 21.7 crores

items.statement: Collections business growing steadily, not hockey-stick; aiming to add large enterprises
items.quote: Collections is a key business for us, but it is a B2B business. So, it's heavy lifting on the ground in terms of working with the enterprise agents to map them to collection centers that we have. So , it's a business that's growing steadily, not a hockey sti ck, but st eadily business growth and we are hoping that we'll continue to grow it

items.statement: CMS business drives higher GTV but lower margin vs other products
items.quote: it's a nature for the product mix due to which because we are doing a CMS business which have kind of a more in terms of G TV standpoint of view but having a lesser margin in comparison to other

items.statement: Legacy business closure cash burn to continue this year and possibly next year; indirect costs to halve from Rs 4.2 cr/quarter
items.quote: We're trying to find solutions where we can, keep the cash burn as minimal as possible, as Sunil mentioned, some numbers, but there is cost to closure.

items.statement: No rush to fundraise; may consider for credit business after model stabilizes and proof-of-concept demonstrated
items.quote: Directionally, there might be need to think about fundraising for the credit business, but something that we are going to come back on. I think right now our focus is to make sure that we drive operating leverage and make sure that many things especially on the credit side, we're able to build products that wor th using our own c apital, maybe work in a some sort of a co-lending model, but initial

items.statement: Debt-free company; borrowings only for treasury operations (OD/FD) to open collection accounts
items.quote: effectively we don't have any debt, only debt or the borrowings, which is coming under the financ ials i s against our OD and FD just for the treasury management, effectively we don't have any debt , we are kind of a debt -free company

items.statement: Holding in Digi Asia Bios Pte Ltd is a little over 3% after rights issue
items.quote: Lalit, it's a little over 3%.

items.statement: Projecting conservative revenue growth of 15% for FY25
items.quote: We are projecting a conservative revenue growth of 15%.

items.statement: Expecting FY25 revenue of INR 2,470-2,480 crores excluding defence
items.quote: The total figure that we are getting it's close to INR 25-30 crores and for defence we have taken only INR 60 crores in that. So it comes to about INR 2,470-2,480 crores.

items.statement: Targeting FY25 EBITDA margin of 11.5% with potential to reach 12%+ by year-end
items.quote: And our internal EBITDA margin is plus 12%, but here we'll like to come in at 11.5%.

items.statement: Repaying INR 90 crores debt in FY25 and INR 80 crores in FY26
items.quote: During this current year, we'll be repaying around INR 90 crores.

items.quote: However, in spite of that, we have been able to maintain our EBITDA levels and improved a bit. So it is around 50 bps-60 bps, we have been able to improve upon the EBITDA level.

items.quote: we have launched the Marygold scheme, in which a consumer can keep accumulating their money, save it with us over a period of six months or nine months and then they can buy it at the end of the tenure and there is a flexible option and a fixed option.
